Hi Susan — quick answers to the security / persistence questions you raised: 

- Vectors persistence: Redwood supports both options. By default, embeddings stored in Redwood-managed encrypted blobstore (soc2-backed) for hosted customers. For customers with PHI or stricter controls, we provide an option to push embeddings to a customer-managed vector DB (S3-compatible snapshots or direct connector to Pinecone/Weaviate/your VDB). We'll note the connector and retention policy in the attached checklist.

- SOC2 & logs: I attached the Geode security questionnaire (geode-security-questions.pdf) with our SOC2 attestation link and a short section on key rotation (KMS-integrated, 90-day rotation recommended). Full audit logs are available for Dedicated / Private with configurable retention.

- Latency estimates (p95 rough):
  • Fast-tier (quantized 8-bit / small model) @ 32 tokens: ~45–70 ms p95 depending on per-request batching
  • Quality-tier (FP16 / 13B class) @ 128 tokens: ~220–350 ms p95; will vary by region and model variant

- mTLS: supported for Redwood Private and Dedicated via customer certs. For hosted customers we can layer IP allowlist + token, or for higher assurance we offer a VPC peering + mTLS option. I'll flag Rishi to provide the exact steps for enabling mTLS in a Private deployment.

Routing policy example (conceptual)
- Region pinning: route by geography header (us-east, eu-west) first.
- Model-tier priority: quality-tier > fast-tier for rerank tasks, but route to fast-tier if latency threshold exceeded.
- Latency-triggered fallback: if request latency > 200ms or queue depth exceeds X, automatically fallback to next-tier.

Example pseudo-policy (human readable):
"""
policy:
  - match: request.region == 'us'
    route:
      - model: quality-tier
        conditions: ["queue_depth < 10", "p95_estimate < 250ms"]
      - model: fast-tier
        conditions: ["always"]
  - match: default
    route: [fast-tier]
"""

Embeddings vs in-model rerank: if you have high cardinality recall and an existing vector DB, I recommend embeddings + lightweight reranker (better cost predictability). If you need single-call simplicity and fewer infra components, in-model rerank is simpler but cost/latency can be higher.

Next steps I recommend:
- Exchange sandbox creds + run small smoke tests (top-10 queries) to validate p95 numbers.
- We can provide a small scripted harness that hits both embeddings+rerank and in-model rerank so you can compare cost/latency side-by-side.
